text:
ali: seeing a weird spike of pod connection drops in eastasia gpupool starting ~06:20 UTC. multiple model pods report 502/connection reset during >1s bursts.
ali: symptoms look like conntrack/NAT exhaustion — tcp syns piling up, kube-proxy logs show SNAT failures, and some pods keep re-resolving egress IPs.
maria: confirmed — I pulled `conntrack -S` on a node and ephemeral port usage is ~98%. nf_conntrack_count ~200k, nf_conntrack_max 262144, but TableEvicted counter increasing fast.
jordan: do we have RDMA nodes in that pool? could be hairpin + prefetcher opening lots of east-west conns.
ali: yes, pool mixes rdma-enabled instances for some model shards. also latest model-prefetcher forked 30+ short-lived connections per request.
maria: stack traces from prefetcher show many short TCP sessions to internal cache: `GET /cache/kv` in <200ms loops.
:devops-bot: [deploy] rollouts/2026-03-18T06:00 -> started canary to gpupool-eastasia
ali: timeline looks aligned with canary scale-up + prefetch change rolled yesterday.
sre-ops: quick mitigation — we can raise nf_conntrack_max and conntrack hashsize on the affected nodes, and add a temporary SNAT pool. but that's bandaid. thoughts?
jordan: agree. Also we should reduce source of short-lived conns: bump keepalive to reuse sockets in prefetcher or switch to HTTP/2 multiplexing.
maria: commands I ran: 
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
echo 262144 > /sys/module/nf_conntrack/parameters/hashsize
conntrack -L | grep SYN | wc -l
```
conntrack GC picked up after raising limits, failures dropped but still noisy.
ali: can we patch kube-proxy to avoid SNAT for pod->pod within same nodepool? a short-term iptables rule to bypass MASQUERADE for known CIDR?
jordan: we can add hairpin SNAT bypass for the model-prefetcher service via `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`? Not ideal. Another option: enable non-snat for PodCIDR in kube-proxy mode, but config change and cluster restart risk.
sre-ops: rolling a per-node sysctl and also nuking the largest offenders (prefetcher replicas) reduced churn. I scaled prefetcher from 60->12 replicas and added a 100ms debounce in the client. immediate drop in ephemeral consumption.
maria: noting evidence: `/proc/net/nf_conntrack` showed many entries with dports in 32768-60999 and expiry ~30s — short TTLs.
network-pager: are we hitting MTU/fragmentation issues on RDMA path? packet loss would increase retransmits and more short connections. but current metrics show very low packet loss, latency stable.
ali: good — not MTU then. main culprit = connection churn + SNAT table pressure.
jordan: long-term: prefer eBPF datapath (Cilium) to remove kube-proxy hairpin SNAT and dramatically reduce conntrack entries. also add a connection pooler inside prefetcher.
sre-ops: action items: 1) keep nf_conntrack increased on pool (done), 2) revert canary prefetcher scale and apply socket reuse patch (doing now), 3) add alert for >85% ephemeral port usage andConntrackEvictions (ticket INFRA-492).
maria: I'll work up a small runbook for oncall: quick sysctl bump, identify top conntrack owners with `conntrack -L | awk '{print $8}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head`, scale down offending deploy, and add temporary iptables MASQ bypass for PodCIDR.
ali: thanks — put the runbook in the ticket and ping infra-oncall. if things re-occur we'll schedule a Cilium trial on a staging gpupool. :thumbsup:
network-pager: also recommending we create a short-term quota on prefetcher concurrent requests to avoid rebuilds at peak.
sre-ops: rolling node-level sysctl out via machine-config now, ETA 4m.
ali: fine — monitoring. will update after stabilization.
(06:28) devops-bot: deployment canary rollback completed: rollouts/2026-03-18T06:00 -> rolled back to stable
jordan: confirmed connection error rate back to baseline at 06:33 UTC.
maria: logging the commands and evidence in INFRA-492. closing thread unless new spikes show up.
